body:
Related: #40425

## Problem

`FileType directory` fires *before* the `BufEnter` path where `dir.lua` populates the buffer, in order to allow a 3P dir-browser plugin to handle the event and (optionally) rename the buffer to e.g. `example:///tmp/foo/`.

But currently, `open_buffer()` continues after `filetypedetect BufRead` as if the original directory buffer is *still* current and valid, which may fall through to the built-in `nvim.dir` path after a 3P plugin ALREADY handled the directory.

## Solution

Keep a buf ref around the early `filetypedetect BufRead` call for directory buffers.

If the `FileType directory` handler switches away from/deletes the original directory buffer, stop the open path instead of continuing into the built-in `nvim.dir` flow.

comment_data.body:
`nvim_buf_get_name` is documented as always returning the absolute path. Could we change it (or confirm) that it always returns a directory with a `/` at the end? 

Then we could just check for that. And we can skip the `fs_state` below, which I think might not be acceptable bc IIUC `match()` is a hotpath. cc @echasnovski @gpanders @clason

> Could we change it (or confirm) that it always returns a directory with a `/` at the end?

It does not use trailing `/` for directory paths for me (on Linux). Changing it would also somewhat go against what is assumed in other places. For example, `vim.fs.normalize` always removes trailing `/`, which I think is reasonable.

This check is indeed costly, as it will read the disk each time filetype detection is made (which can be fairly frequent in plugins that rely on `vim.filetype.match()`). And `vim.filetype.match()` is designed to be as fast as possible. At least until there is something like #30086, I'd say this check adds too much overhead.

comment_data.body: just trying to follow: why didn't we do this in the other PR? just an oversight?

What does `handle the |FileType| event for "directory" to take ownership of local directory buffers` mean *exactly*? What needs to be done to prevent `dir.lua` taking over?

Looking at the test, my guess is that `vim.api.nvim_buf_delete(ev.buf, { force = true })` is the suggested approach? If yes, then this is very problematic: wiping out a buffer can affect window layout, triggers events, might be bad as it is done in the autocommand for this buffer, etc.

My expectation is that there has to be a way to disable `dir.lua` entirely during runtime. Deleting autocommand is a fine approach. Setting some flag that is recognized by `dir.lua` itself when it tries to take over `ft=directory` buffer is also fine.

comment_regular_data.body:
OK, so `vim.filetype.match()` should not stat paths on every call (at least for right now) - that makes sense. Also, I do not want this to be blocked by #30086 (not only is it under contentious discussion, but I want dir.lua overriding to be handled relatively quickly, for the sake of mini.files and beyond).

I reverted to the directory check from `vim.filetype.match()`.

I moved the check back to the core directory-open path. This keeps the hotpath unchanged while still letting `FileType directory` be the earlier dispatch point for actual directory buffers.

If this is not a satisfiable solution I'm seeking advice...

The `open_buffer` approach is worth considering, but it introduces a new order-of-operations question(s), so it seems preferable to avoid it.

It seems to me that if `b_ffname` (aka `nvim_buf_get_name`) [ensures that directory buffers](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40529#discussion_r3512550132) ends with `/`, that has broad long-term value. (And i don't care much that `fnamemodify()` has traditionally removed the trailing slash, though for back-compat that particular function can't be changed)

Can you spare me some more context on the long-term value of this? Generally, it seems like just as often as it's more idiomatic for paths to end in `/` it's more idiomatic for them not to.

Is the idea here to change the internal and external representation of directories with the invariant of having trailing `/`? So apis like `vim.fs.normalize()` (that echasnovski mentioned earlier) have a trailing `/`? Would this be a breaking change anywhere?

I do like this idea but seeking a bit of clarification here - AFAIK this change would span a meaty bit of the codebase (not that this makes it any less right, ofc). I think for sure the internal and external representation of directories HAS to match (i.e. have trailing slash or not, one or the other).

> it seems like just as often as it's more idiomatic for paths to end in `/` it's more idiomatic for them not to.

when they end with `/` it is useful because it saves an `isdirectory()` check.



> Is the idea here to change the internal and external representation of directories with the invariant of having trailing `/`? So apis like `vim.fs.normalize()` (that echasnovski mentioned earlier) have a trailing `/`? Would this be a breaking change anywhere?

it doesn't need to change `vim.fs.normalize()` nor `fnamemodify()` (and they already do work to drop the `/` , so they won't need to adapt either way). 

it only requires a change to `b_ffname` , which will then reflect in `nvim_buf_get_name`. however, if changing `b_ffname` ends up being a huge problem, then we could decide to selectively change `nvim_buf_get_name` . or retreat :)
the PR desc here seems outdated?
is this at least an incremental improvement, or do you have blocking concerns @echasnovski  ?

> is this at least an incremental improvement, or do you have blocking concerns @echasnovski ?

The "wipeout directory buffer to not have `dir.lua` act on it" suggestion - not an improvement for reasons [described here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40529#discussion_r3564881677).

The actual code change - I don't feel qualified to judge. My best guess is that it allows to wipeout the buffer during `FileType` detect event? If yes, then this feels like opening more problems (like behavior of other buffer events and `FileType` autocommands if the buffer was wiped out) than enabling solutions.

> My best guess is that it allows to wipeout the buffer during FileType detect event?

I want to avoid superfluous discussion but this is not the case. Look at the provided prospective mini.nvim snippet [here](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/pull/2493#issuecomment-4948174358) (justin, might want to take a look to to ensure that we're on the same page). 

The whole point of this pr is to make `FileType directory` fire before the `BufEnter` path where `dir.lua` calls try_open() and _populates the buffer then_. What, if anything, is insufficient about this approach (besides the lack of clarity of how to "mark" a directory as claimed)?

In the spirit of [this approach](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/40697#issuecomment-4951335186), I have removed documentation of how to "work" with dir.lua and will re-add it once the autocmd deletion approach is implemented.

Otherwise, this pr is ready as it stands.

> Otherwise, this pr is ready as it stands.

The whole point of this PR seems to enable "delete directory buffer to prevent `dir.lua` from handling it" approach. Which is redundant in light of "delete `nvim.dir` augroup to prevent `dir.lua` from handling all directory buffers".

> ... will re-add it once the autocmd deletion approach is implemented.

There is nothing left to implement. The functionality [already uses `nvim.dir` augroup](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/58b6310adc938f49ea85e6ab4839616f8af28ecd/runtime/plugin/dir.lua#L42). The only thing left is to decide to use this approach (seems established), document it, and possibly test (to prevent accidental breaking of third-party plugins).

> The whole point of this PR seems to enable "delete directory buffer to prevent dir.lua from handling it" approach. Which is redundant in light of "delete nvim.dir augroup to prevent dir.lua from handling all directory buffers".

1. This is not the case. This provides a path so that `dir.lua` itself can hook into the `FileType directory` handler, which has been established as desirable. Also, see [this comment](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40529#issuecomment-4951723166) that I just unhid with respect to "buffer deletion".

> There is nothing left to implement.

2. While technically true for your desired functionality, this is not entirely the case. There are some rough edges with how this should interact with the `-` keymap that I'll get to ASAP after this PR (just want it to be properly documented when it's appropriately implemented). Once again sorry for the delay on this.

@justinmk

> The whole point of this pr is to make `FileType directory` fire before the `BufEnter` path where `dir.lua` calls try_open() and _populates the buffer then_.

that sentence seems helpful in the problem/solution, and maybe delete some of the other excursive notes in it.

also would be very helpful just to have a tiny, concrete example, like:

```
3P dir browser plugin does ...
buffer is renamed to "..."
```

i.e. make the actual real-world use-case clear. the descriptions here and in the test-name are too abstract.

See the updated and clarified PR.

Presumably, after this, a follow-up would flesh out autocmd deletion semantics as well as the corresponding documentation & tests to outline a canonical way to work with dir.lua as outlined in #40697

> This lets a plugin directory browser handle a local directory path like `/tmp/foo/` and switch to its own browser buffer, for example `example:///tmp/foo/`.

This is not really an encouraged pattern imo, nor the main purpose of `FileType directory`. Rather the main purpose is that dir browser plugins can just... listen to that event and handle it. The fact that some of them love to rename the buffer is just something we live with.

> This is not really an encouraged pattern imo, nor the main purpose of `FileType directory`. Rather the main purpose is that dir browser plugins can just... listen to that event and handle it. The fact that some of them love to rename the buffer is just something we live with.

why did this get merged if this behavior is not actually encouraged? would it not be healthier for neovim's development if plugins had to adapt over the release cycle?

oh okay thank god :sweat_smile: 

thnx for the clarification<3
